subject: Rapidsync MAP: performance evaluation scope and SLOs
messages:
From: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@rapidsync.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.menon@rapidsync.ai>
Date: 2026-09-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Rapidsync MAP: performance eval kickoff

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with latency and routing concepts. We want to get the MAP formalized so we can close the procurement window in late October. Key ask: finalize the performance benchmarking plan and acceptance SLOs for the Rapidsync pilot (primary concerns: TTFT spikes during cold start, p95 latency under load, and concurrency behavior during business-hours bursts).

Quick context on current production profile: ~30 req/s sustained during steady hours, 400 concurrent sessions at peak (10:00–11:00 PST), payloads average 512 tokens per request, 95th token-length ~1,200 tokens for longer transcripts. We expect a small set of heavy requests (10% of traffic) that exercise long-context generation.

Can you send a clear scoping doc with: workload slices, exact metrics (TTFT, p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec throughput), cold vs warm runs, concurrency plan, pass/fail criteria, and an estimated time window to run the acceptance tests? Also confirm whether Redwood will run runs on Hosted API or Dedicated for the pilot, and what model/quantization baseline you'll use for the results.

We attached a short sample of representative requests (workload_samples.jsonl) and a first-draft MAP spreadsheet outlining milestones. If possible, we want a test run the week of 2026-09-22.

Thanks — Oliver
Oliver Chen
Head of ML Ops, Rapidsync

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@rapidsync.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Rapidsync MAP: performance eval kickoff

Hi Oliver / Priya,

Appreciate the context — attached is our proposed benchmarking scope and acceptance matrix (rapidsync_map_v1.xlsx) and a short TTFT/SLO primer (ttft_slo_matrix.pdf). High-level summary below; full details are in the attachment.

Benchmark scope (workload slices):
- Slice A (baseline production): 30 req/s sustained, 400 concurrency bursts (10m windows), 512 tokens avg payload.
- Slice B (stress long-context): 10 req/s steady with 10% heavy requests at ~1,200 tokens — validates KV cache and memory paths.
- Slice C (peak shock): short 20-minute ramp to 1,000 concurrent connections (simulate spike during campaign).

Metrics to capture: TTFT (wall-clock to first token), p50/p95/p99 and p99.9 latency per response, tokens/sec throughput (aggregate), GPU utilization, and end-to-end cost estimate ($/1M tokens) for the run. We'll also capture cold-start vs warmed-KV metrics (first 50 requests after a model instance spin-up and after 30m idle).

SLO / acceptance criteria (proposed):
- Canary gate (canary run in Dedicated): p95 <= 350 ms, TTFT <= 120 ms, no functional errors >0.05%
- Pilot acceptance (full MAP acceptance): p95 <= 450 ms, p99 <= 1.2 s, median latency aligned with canary, sustained throughput matching slice A within 10% of target token rate
- Concurrency resilience: sustained 5-minute windows at target concurrency with error rate <0.1% and no >20% degradation in p95 compared to baseline.

Execution plan / test windows:
- Prep: we need a short account key and a sandbox endpoint (we can run on Dedicated test pool or Hosted with reserved capacity). Please confirm preference — Dedicated is recommended for predictable throughput.
- Dry run: 30–60 min to validate harness and dataset (we replay your workload_samples.jsonl with header-level throttles).
- Acceptance runs: three runs per slice (cold/warm/cold) across two model variants (baseline fp16 and quantized int8) to show tradeoffs. Expected elapsed time per full acceptance pass: ~5 hours.

Attachments: rapidsync_map_v1.xlsx (timeline + acceptance matrix), ttft_slo_matrix.pdf, workload_samples.jsonl (your upload).

Next steps: confirm Dedicated vs Hosted, share the sandbox API key or a short-term CIDR allowlist, and confirm target test date (you suggested week of 9/22). We'll slot an engineer and product owner for the run and deliver a short results deck within 48 hours of completion.

CC-ing Vanessa (AE) and Marissa (Product) to lock down schedule and model baselines.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-16T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Rapidsync MAP: performance eval kickoff

Quick note from product: a couple of recommendations to reduce iteration risk during the pilot:
- For the canary, target p95 <= 350 ms (as Neha proposed) but require a separate validation of KV-cache warmup behavior: track p95 for first 5 minutes after instance creation and after a 30-minute idle; flag if p95 increases >30%.
- Recommend Dedicated test pool using H100-80G if available (we've seen more consistent TTFT on H100 vs A100 for long-context workloads). If customer cannot access H100, we will still run on A100 but will include a normalized performance delta in the report.
- Add a stress eviction test: sustained 10-minute run at 1,200 concurrency to validate cache eviction and queueing; include memory/oom monitoring.

I'll prepare a short config snippet for the load generator and push to the Drive folder referenced in the MAP.

—Marissa
Product Lead, Performance

From: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@rapidsync.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.menon@rapidsync.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-17T15:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Rapidsync MAP: performance eval kickoff

Neha / team — this looks good, thanks. Rapidsync confirms Dedicated pool preferred and we can open a short-term CIDR allowlist for the test window. We accept the SLOs you proposed; two small asks before we schedule:
1) Can you include cost delta estimates between fp16 and int8 quantized runs for our procurement pack?
2) Please include a short paragraph in the final MAP about expected mitigations if the canary misses the p95 gate (recommended fallbacks, model variant switch, and temporary rate-limiting thresholds).

We'd like the full acceptance run on 2026-09-22 starting 10:00 PST. Please confirm availability and provide a calendar invite.

Oliver
Oliver Chen
Head of ML Ops, Rapidsync
oliver.chen@rapidsync.ai
